title: Chandigarh University's CUBIC Partners with 247VC to Expand Investment Framework for Deep-Tech Startups - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Chandigarh University's CUBIC signed an MoU with VC firm 247VC Investment Trust at PRAGATI Q-Foundry 2026 to create a funding and mentorship pipeline for quantum and deep-tech startups under India's National Quantum Mission.

insights.claim: CUBIC at Chandigarh University signed an MoU with 247VC Investment Trust at the PRAGATI Q-Foundry 2026 meet in New Delhi, creating a structured investment and mentorship pipeline for startups in the university's incubation ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Another sign Indian academic incubators are being wired to venture capital under the NQM.
insights.locator: has executed a Memorandum of Understanding

insights.claim: CUBIC will identify eligible seed- and early-stage ventures in quantum computing, sensing, communications and photonics for deal flow, pitch sessions and due diligence with 247VC and its syndicate networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Deal flow is scoped to early-stage quantum, so only small tickets are implied; no amounts are disclosed.

insights.claim: PRAGATI Q-Foundry 2026, run under India's National Quantum Mission and the Ministry of Science and Technology, aims to move academic quantum research toward industrial validation, co-development and commercial deployment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government-sponsored translation programs are building India's domestic quantum startup pipeline.

insights.claim: The framework helps spin-offs prepare financial projections, IP documentation, demo days and angel/family-office introductions, and assists with institutional pitch materials, IP valuation models and follow-on capital.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The value is in investor-readiness for university spin-offs, which often lack IP valuation capability.

insights.claim: CUBIC's mandate extends beyond quantum to semiconductor design, integrated photonics, advanced materials and robotics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The pipeline is a broad deep-tech funnel, not a quantum-only vehicle.
